title: One request through the API server
summary: A create request passes each stage before it is stored.

steps.n: kubectl sends a create request with its credentials over TLS to the API server.
The API server checks the certificate or token and works out the user and groups.
RBAC decides whether this user may create this resource in this namespace.
A mutating webhook adds default labels and a sidecar before validation sees the object.
The object is checked against its schema and policy, then written to etcd as one transaction.
The scheduler sees the new unscheduled pod through its watch and starts placing it.

title: Failure and recovery: a webhook blocks the cluster
summary: A policy webhook with no backend stops every pod from being created.

steps.n: A developer creates a pod and the API server accepts it through authentication and authorization.
The API server calls the validating webhook, which has no healthy endpoint behind its service.
The call times out and failurePolicy Fail turns the timeout into a refusal.
The developer sees an internal error naming the webhook and every other team sees the same.
The operator reads the error, sees the webhook name and finds its pods were evicted.
They exclude system namespaces and the webhook itself, then restore its pods.
Pod creation succeeds again and an alert is added for webhook availability.

title: List once, then watch
summary: A client avoids polling by watching from a resource version.

steps.n: The controller asks for all pods once and notes the returned resourceVersion.
The API server reads the current state and revision from etcd or its own watch cache.
The controller stores the list in a local cache so later reads cost no API calls.
It opens a watch starting from the version it saw, so it receives only changes.
A modified event arrives for one pod and updates the cache.
The changed object key is added to a work queue for the reconcile loop.

title: Failure and recovery: a lost update
summary: Two writers collide and the second uses the conflict to recover.

steps.n: Writer A reads a ConfigMap at version 41 and prepares a change.
Writer B reads the same ConfigMap at version 41 and prepares a different change.
A sends its update with version 41 and the API server accepts it as version 42.
The write is committed to etcd and watchers are told about version 42.
B sends its update with version 41 and the API server rejects it with a 409 conflict.
B re-reads version 42 from the API and merges its change on top of A.
B sends the merged object with version 42 and it is stored as version 43.

title: How a write commits in etcd
summary: A write commits when a majority has stored it.

steps.n: The API server sends a put request to the etcd leader.
The leader writes the entry to its own log and flushes it to disk.
The leader sends the entry to follower A.
The leader sends the entry to follower B at the same time.
Follower A stores the entry and confirms, which gives a majority of two out of three.
The leader commits the entry and tells the API server the write succeeded.

title: Failure and recovery: losing quorum
summary: Two of three members fail and writes stop until one returns.

steps.n: All three members agree and member 1 is the leader.
The node of member 2 loses power and its disk is not reachable.
The second failure in the same zone leaves only member 1 running.
Member 1 cannot reach a majority, so it refuses writes and the API server returns timeouts.
Running pods are unaffected because the kubelets already have their specs.
The operator restarts one failed node and etcd elects a leader again.
Health checks pass and the team spreads members across three zones afterwards.

title: Compact and defragment
summary: Free space step by step without taking etcd down.

steps.n: An alert reports the database size at ninety percent of its quota.
The operator reads the current revision and database size from endpoint status.
They compact to the current revision, which discards old key versions.
They defragment one follower first and wait for it to become healthy again.
They defragment the other follower, then the leader last, one at a time.
They disarm any alarm and confirm the size dropped before ending the change.

title: Failure and recovery: etcd is full
summary: Writes fail with NOSPACE and the right order restores them.

steps.n: A controller updates an object thousands of times a minute in a bug loop.
Each update creates a new revision and the database fills its quota.
etcd raises NOSPACE and the API server starts returning errors for writes.
The operator compacts and defragments members one by one to release space.
They disarm the alarm so writes are accepted again.
They find and fix the looping controller, because more quota would only delay the next alarm.
A new alert fires at seventy percent of quota so the next time there is a full day to react.

title: Filter, score and bind
summary: The scheduler narrows nodes and picks the best one.

steps.n: A new pod with no node name is seen by the scheduler.
Nodes without enough memory, with an untolerated taint or the wrong label are removed.
Three nodes pass and move to scoring.
Each node receives a score for spreading, image locality and resource balance.
The scheduler writes the binding for the highest scoring node to the API server.
The pod now has a node name and the kubelet on that node picks it up.

title: Failure and recovery: nothing fits
summary: A pod stays Pending until the cause in the event is fixed.

steps.n: A pod requests sixteen cores while the largest node has eight.
Every node is rejected for insufficient CPU.
A FailedScheduling event says zero of six nodes are available with the reasons per node.
The developer describes the pod and reads the reason instead of guessing.
The operator decides between a smaller request and a larger node group.
The request is set to the measured four cores and the pod is applied again.
The scheduler binds the pod and the Pending state ends.

title: The reconcile loop
summary: A controller replaces a missing pod without being told.

steps.n: The informer reports that one pod of a ReplicaSet was deleted.
The controller counts matching pods from its cache and finds two instead of three.
It creates one new pod object to restore the desired count.
The scheduler assigns the pod and the kubelet starts it.
The kubelet reports the pod as ready to the API server.
The controller updates the ReplicaSet status to three ready replicas.

title: Failure and recovery: a leader is lost
summary: Another copy takes over when a lease is not renewed.

steps.n: Manager 1 is the leader and renews its lease every few seconds.
The API server slows down and the renewal of the lease does not complete in time.
Manager 2 sees the lease was not renewed within its duration.
Manager 2 writes itself as holder and starts running the controllers.
Manager 1 fails its next renewal and stops its controllers to avoid acting twice.
Many transitions in an hour raise an alert that points at API server latency.
The team fixes the slow storage behind the API server and transitions stop.

title: From pod spec to running container
summary: The kubelet turns a pod spec into containers.

steps.n: The kubelet sees a pod bound to its node through its watch.
It asks the runtime to create the pod sandbox that holds the network namespace.
The runtime calls the CNI plugin, which creates the interface and assigns the pod IP.
The kubelet asks the storage driver to attach and mount the requested volumes.
Init containers run first and then the app containers are started in order.
The kubelet runs probes and reports the pod as Running and Ready to the API server.

title: Failure and recovery: a node goes NotReady
summary: A stopped runtime makes the node unhealthy and the fix is found bottom up.

steps.n: The container runtime crashes after an update and stops answering.
The kubelet cannot report healthy status, so the node lease goes stale.
After the grace period the node controller marks the node NotReady and taints it.
The operator reads the kubelet journal and sees repeated runtime connection errors.
crictl fails, which shows the problem is the runtime and not the kubelet.
They restart the runtime, enable it at boot and confirm crictl lists containers again.
The kubelet reports ready, the taint is removed and pods are scheduled again.

title: Diagnose from the symptom
summary: Match the symptom to the component before changing anything.

steps.n: Pods stay Pending with no events and existing pods are fine.
No events means the scheduler never evaluated them, so start there.
The scheduler log shows repeated lease renewal errors.
The errors point to slow API server responses caused by etcd disk latency.
They move etcd to local SSD storage and the latency drops.
New pods are scheduled within seconds and an alert guards disk latency.

title: Failure and recovery: the API server is down
summary: Work from the node when kubectl is not available.

steps.n: Every command fails, but the applications still serve traffic.
On a control plane node the kubelet is running and shows the API server container exited.
crictl ps -a shows the API server restarting and its log mentions a bad flag.
The static pod manifest has a typo from an edit made an hour ago.
The kubelet notices the manifest changed and starts a fresh API server container within a few seconds.
They restore the saved manifest and the kubelet recreates the API server pod.
kubectl works again, etcd is healthy and a rule is added to copy manifests before edits.
